# The next number of T below a value

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `next_down` · proved for finite operands · proved for infinite and NaN operands · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The next number of `T` below $a$, for every value of `T`:

$$r = \mathrm{pred}(a).$$

## C++

**Not yet called by the public headers.** No public operation computes this kernel yet.

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r = \mathrm{pred}(a)$: the next number of the format below $a$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `next_down_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/EntryKernels.v), against `next_down_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions next_down_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition next_down_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  let r := next_down emin prec a in
  fmt emin prec r /\
  r = pred radix2 (FLT_exp emin prec) a.
```

## Infinite and NaN operands

The statement above is about finite operands. The claims also say what the kernel returns when its operands may be infinite or NaN. That statement requires:

- $a$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

and then:

- $r$ is the next number of `T` below $a$: for a finite $a$ the largest number of `T` below it, $-\infty$ below $-\Omega$ and $-\eta$ below either zero; $\Omega$ for $a = +\infty$; $-\infty$ for $a = -\infty$; a NaN for a NaN.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

**Status of this statement:** proved. Rocq checks the theorem `next_down_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeEntry.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeEntry.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions next_down_ieee_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proofs of `next_down_correct` and `next_down_ieee_correct` depend on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** IEEE 754 nextDown on the bit pattern (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/next_down.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/next_down.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# IEEE 754 nextDown: the next number of the format below a, on every input (milestone2.md,
# "next_up and next_down on every input"). A NaN gives a NaN; -inf gives -inf; the most negative
# finite number gives -inf; a positive number the previous one toward zero, a negative one the
# previous one away from zero; either zero the most negative subnormal number; +inf the largest
# finite number. Computed on the bit pattern, without a floating-point operation.

r = pred(a)
```

## Measured

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements of the statement on infinite and NaN operands.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
